summary: Notepad++ is a genuine, widely used, actively maintained free editor that has existed since 2003. It is led by one maintainer with no legal entity. Its updater was hijacked in 2025 by a suspected state actor, and 2026 saw many CVEs. Handling was transparent and fixes were quick. Enterprises can use it with controls.
green_flags: More than 20 years of continuous development, with active 8.9.x releases and wide adoption [E3, E11]
Transparent incident disclosure and a hardened update process [E2, E5]
Free for commercial use under the GPL [E8]
No regulatory or legal misconduct found [E9]
yellow_flags: Single lead maintainer, no corporate entity or SLA, and a recent state-sponsored update-hijack supply-chain compromise [E2, E3]
Many 2026 CVEs, including code execution, and no SECURITY.md [E1, E7]
Code signing lapsed in 2025 and a self-signed certificate was used until 8.8.7 [E6]
Lookalike and impersonation sites make the download source a risk [E10]
reasoning:
There is no deception, misconduct or abandonment, so the product is not RED. A normal procurement process is not enough, though. A single maintainer, a recent supply-chain compromise and frequent 2026 CVEs mean a buyer should add compensating controls: pin and test the latest patched version, deploy through managed software distribution, disable or proxy the auto-updater, download only from official sources, and verify signatures. That makes it YELLOW.

Adversarial review: Notepad++ is a legitimate, widely used and actively maintained open-source editor. Nothing RED-grade was found. The vendor's own conduct is clean, and the supply-chain compromise was done to the project and handled transparently. The recent incident with a single maintainer still leaves a single point of failure, and 2026 CVEs and the code-signing lapse add risk. A buyer would need compensating controls: pin versions, use managed deployment, control the auto-updater and download only from official sources. That makes YELLOW the right verdict.

claims.claim: Notepad++ has been maintained since 2003 by Don Ho and is actively released (8.9.x in 2026)
The update mechanism was hardened after the 2025 compromise (signed and verified updates) and is described by the project as effectively unexploitable
claims.note: This is the project's own claim. It was reported by The Register and Privacy Guides and has not been independently audited.

claims.claim: The software is free for any use, including commercial

findings.finding: The update channel was hijacked via a hosting-provider compromise from about June to Dec 2025, with targeted malware delivery, and was later hardened. In 2026 there were many further CVEs, including code-execution and installer issues in 8.9.x, and the repository has no SECURITY.md. The disclosure and fixes were reasonably transparent and fast, but the incident is recent and the patch cadence is high [E1, E2, E5, E7].

The project depends on one lead maintainer, Don Ho, with community contributors. It has run since 2003 with continuous releases, but the bus factor and single point of failure remain, now combined with a recent supply-chain compromise [E3, E4].
There is no corporate legal entity or contractual vendor. Lookalike and impersonation sites are common, so downloads must come only from the official domain or GitHub [E10].

There is no SLA, vendor support or formal certification. Code-signing lapsed in 2025 before being restored in 8.8.7. Enterprises should pin versions, deploy through managed channels, and manage the auto-updater [E6, E8].
No regulatory action or lawsuit against the project was found. The only item is a May 2026 trademark dispute over an unofficial macOS port, which ended in a rename [E9].
A single maintainer combined with a supply-chain compromise that ended less than a year ago is a bus-factor and single-point-of-failure risk, even though it was well handled.

challenges: Checked whether anything RED-grade was missed. The evidence shows no regulator or court misconduct, no deception and no abandonment. The only legal item is a trademark dispute over an unofficial macOS port.

Checked whether YELLOW was only 'not much found'. It was not. The product is plainly real and maintained, but a state-sponsored update-channel hijack ran from June to December 2025. Code signing lapsed and was replaced by a self-signed certificate. Many 2026 CVEs include code-execution issues. Lead-maintainer dependence remains.

Checked the incident handling. Disclosure was transparent and the update process was hardened, so this is not RED. The project's 'effectively unexploitable' claim is its own and unaudited. There is no SECURITY.md and no independent audit.
No new searches were run. The evidence summary was enough to decide, and extra searches were unlikely to change the verdict.
